Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testTruncateLang59` in `DateUtilsTest` is failing because the `DateUtils.truncate` method is buggy when dealing with DST (Daylight Saving Time) switching hours. The bug occurs when trying to truncate a date in Mountain Daylight Time (MDT) by hour and getting a result in Mountain Standard Time (MST), which is one hour off from the expected output.

1. The test case sets the TimeZone to Mountain Time (MST7MDT) and creates a date `oct31_01MDT` representing October 31, 2004, at 01:00:00 MDT.
2. It then demonstrates the problem by creating a Calendar instance `gval` and setting the minutes to the same value as a part of the test setup.
3. The test attempts to truncate the date `oct31_01_02_03_04MDT` by seconds using `DateUtils.truncate` method.
4. The expected behavior is to truncate the date accurately, but due to the DST switching hours bug, the result is incorrect.

Based on the description in the bug report and the observed behavior in the failing test, it is likely that the issue lies in the implementation of the `DateUtils.truncate` method not handling DST switching hours correctly.

Next, I will identify and inspect the relevant code snippet of the `DateUtils` class to further investigate the root cause of the bug.
